ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: Flash loan -> CLOB self-trade -> AMM reads distorted state
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB and AMM pools have independent pricing state. CLOB is a transfer handler, not a pricing oracle. AMM pool types compute prices from their own state (sqrtPriceX96 per pool). No shared state to distort.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H2: snapPrice in addLiquidity allows arbitrary price movement -> sandwich
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: snapPrice reverts with DynamicPool__PriceCannotSnapWithLiquidity if ANY liquidity exists between current and target price (DynamicHelper.sol:246). Sandwich requires liquidity to extract from, contradicting snap requirement. Only called during addLiquidity behind reentrancy guard.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H3: SingleProviderPoolType trusts external pricing hook -> oracle spoof
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook is set at pool creation by pool creator (who is also the LP). Price bounded by MIN_SQRT_RATIO/MAX_SQRT_RATIO (SingleProviderPoolType.sol:311). A malicious hook only hurts the pool creator's own funds. Users who trade on that pool accept the hook's pricing.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H4: Direct swap bypasses pricing bounds checked by hooks
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Direct swap is by design: executor provides swap amount (OTC market-making). Protected by maxAmountOut (AMMModule.sol:1852), minAmountIn (line 1925), reentrancy guard, deadline validation, and before/after swap hooks. Not a bypass - different swap mode.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5: Oracle returns stale price -> buy cheap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: No external oracle dependency in core AMM math. DynamicPoolType uses internal sqrtPriceX96. FixedPoolType uses constant ratio. SingleProviderPoolType calls hook per-swap (not cached). No staleness vector.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H6: Oracle read has no bounds -> feed extreme price
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Same as H3. Only external price source is hook. Price bounded by MIN_SQRT_RATIO/MAX_SQRT_RATIO. At extreme valid prices, math produces bounded outputs (near-zero or reserve-capped).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H7: TWAP window is short -> manipulate cheaply
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: No TWAP oracle exists in this protocol. No observation array, no cumulative price tracking, no TWAP computation. Unlike Uniswap V3 which has Oracle.sol, Limit Break AMM has no price accumulator.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H8: Read stale oracle -> front-run update
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: No external oracle update mechanism. SingleProviderPoolType calls hook.getPoolPriceForSwap() fresh on every swap (not cached). No update transaction to front-run.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H9: Controlled hook returns fake sqrtPriceX96
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook controlled by pool creator = LP. Attacker cannot change another pool's hook. Creating own pool with malicious hook only drains own funds. Trust model: pool creator sets hook, users opt in.

Slippage and deadline enforced at AMMModule level (not pool type). Input swaps check amountOut >= limitAmount. Output swaps check amountIn <= limitAmount. Direct swaps check maxAmountOut and minAmountIn. No pool type can bypass these.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C26: Cetus precision extraction ($223M) - overflow in computeRatioX96
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow (not exploitable near-zero). TickMath enforces MIN_TICK/MAX_TICK bounds. getSqrtPriceAtTick reverts on out-of-bounds ticks. getAmount0Delta at MIN_SQRT_RATIO gives bounded amounts.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C27: Balancer rounding direction ($128M) - dust swaps drain pool
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 1000 dust swaps (1 wei each) show pool balance is non-negative after. Rounding consistently favors protocol: input amountOut uses mulDiv (rounds down), output amountIn uses mulDivRoundingUp (rounds up).

Not applicable to concentrated liquidity. Each position tracks its own liquidity units (not shares). No share inflation possible. getAmount0Delta with liquidity=1 gives small bounded amounts. Second depositor gets proportional amounts.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C29: Hook price manipulation - Balancer rate provider ($128M)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SingleProviderPoolType validates MIN_SQRT_RATIO <= price < MAX_SQRT_RATIO. At extreme prices: price=0 gives zero output (guarded), price=1 gives zero output, MIN_SQRT_RATIO gives near-zero output. Not exploitable for inflation.
Fuzz tested with 25 random (amountIn, fee) pairs. SwapMath.computeSwapByInputStep always loses value on round-trip due to fees and rounding. Deterministic test also confirms.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C1-C2: FullMath.mulDiv edge cases and rounding direction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Tested mulDiv(max,max,max), mulDiv(0,x,y), mulDivRoundingUp >= mulDiv for all inputs. phantom overflow handled correctly. Rounding up always >= rounding down.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C17: FeeHelper fee conservation - input fees can never exceed input
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fuzz tested: fee = mulDiv(input, BPS, MAX_BPS) always <= input. Conservation holds: remaining + fees == original. Output fee uses mulDivRoundingUp (rounds against user). 100% fee asymmetry is by design.
CLOB uses mulDivRoundingUp (rounds against taker, favoring maker). Max difference from floor is 2 wei. Rounding direction is consistent across fuzz testing.

theft_theses.thesis: Flash loan -> CLOB self-trade at extreme price -> AMM reads distorted CLOB state -> extract on AMM at wrong price
Sandwich around snapPrice to extract value from price movement during addLiquidity
Deploy malicious hook to SingleProviderPoolType to spoof oracle pricing and extract value
Use directSwap to bypass pricing bounds and swap at arbitrary prices
Exploit stale oracle price to buy cheap and sell at real price
Feed extreme price via oracle to extract via arbitrage against bounded venues
Manipulate short TWAP window to profit from contracts using TWAP
Front-run oracle update to extract delta between stale and fresh price
Control hook to return fake sqrtPriceX96 and swap at rigged price
Bypass slippage/deadline params to execute swap at worse price and capture difference
